figures.before: GMP Defined: What It Is, What It Isn't, and Why It's Different from Fixed-Price and Cost-Plus
figures.alt: Construction planning table with drawings, measuring tools, a blank clipboard, and coordination materials
figures.caption: A GMP needs an understandable cost basis: scope, documents, allowances, contingencies, assumptions, schedule, procurement, general conditions, and the process that governs unresolved work.

figures.before: Why GMP Is Standard in Hospital, Institutional, and Large Commercial Construction
figures.alt: Hospital life-safety coordination area with protected egress route, temporary construction separation, and clearly maintained corridor access
figures.caption: Complex institutional work benefits from early cost and construction planning because the operating constraints, phasing, life-safety controls, procurement, and required decisions do not wait for a simple bid package.

figures.before: Open-Book Cost Auditing: What It Means in Practice
figures.alt: Contractor qualification documents, insurance verification, and a blank checklist organized on a clean desk
figures.caption: Open-book review means the owner can trace the basis of the budget and the changes to it through documented scopes, bids, allowances, contingencies, buyout decisions, and records that can be checked.
